Angela Walker was the second of the marathon team to head off down the considerably shorter 2.995 mile course. Her task was to pull up one or two places and bring the Belles nearer to their top 15 target.

We have already made a good start a few weeks ago, with the men's team winning the Surrey Road Relays for the first time since 1997 and our ladies winning bronze, with Angela Walker setting a new course record on the way.

While David Anderson was setting the fastest men's time, Angela Walker was doing a similar job on stage one in the women's race. It's a shame, in a way, that the women's race is held at the same time as the men's, because the outstanding women's runs tend to get buried in the pack.

Angela Walker stepped in to head the A team off, after Getenesh revealed she was feeling very tired. With a marathon, a triathlon and a Surrey relay course record under her belt in the previous weeks Angela was happy to take on the additional challenge, although admits to finding the course tough.

Erica Fogg started off strongly for the women's team and set the pace for the Belles right from the start, but Angela Walker wasn't going to let her out of her sight and with a water bottle tucked into her belt (she was suffering from a sore throat), she kept the team momentum going.

With conditions cold and overcast Angela Walker braved the scramble for the start and headed off in the middle of the pack. Not helped by a trip and a push at the top corner, Angela dug in and showed her usual tough approach to racing.
